name: Jacobin
summary: Jacobinism is the revolutionary republicanism of the Jacobin Club and its Montagnard leaders, above all Robespierre. It held that sovereignty lies in the people and is indivisible, that a centralised republic should be defended by civic virtue and, in crisis, by terror, and that property and wealth should serve the public good without abolishing private ownership.
scope: The Montagnard Jacobins of 1793-94 around Robespierre and Saint-Just, based on Robespierre's 1793 declaration of rights and 1794 report on political morality, the Constitution of 1793 and reference accounts. Excludes the pre-1792 constitutional monarchist club, Girondins, and later uses of 'Jacobin' for any centralist.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The 1793 Constitution added a right to public assistance, which supports state-guaranteed care for those in need.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The Jacobin maximum also capped wages, so there is no clear stance; inferred.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Generally pro-market in principle, but the Jacobins imposed general price maxima and requisitions when markets failed in wartime.

public-ownership.rationale: No program of nationalizing industries; wartime state direction was an emergency measure.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Robespierre proposed exempting those below subsistence and progressive taxation by size of fortune.

unions-good.rationale: The republic recognised citizens, not corporate bodies, and capped wages; inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: The 1793 Constitution guaranteed property, yet Robespierre limited it by the duty to respect others' rights and the right to existence.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Inferred from state control of commerce as a source of public wealth.

cut-welfare.rationale: The 1793 Constitution recognised public assistance as a social debt.

worker-ownership.rationale: Robespierre called community of goods a chimera; wide property for individuals, not collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: The Law of Suspects authorised detention on vague suspicion in defence of the Republic.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; no basis to infer a position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Speech against the Republic was prosecuted as counterrevolutionary, though hate speech as such was not the issue.

strong-leader.rationale: Rule was by committees of the Convention, and Robespierre cast his rule as virtue serving the people, not a personal leader bypassing it.

state-harmful.rationale: Jacobinism centres on a sovereign, indivisible public authority over civil society.

limit-guns.rationale: The levee en masse and citizen armies relied on an armed people; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: A strong security apparatus and army defended the Republic; inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Republican virtue was central to Jacobin politics; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Jacobins built a strong centralised government and defended indivisible sovereignty.

rehabilitation.rationale: Terror was justice that is prompt, severe and inflexible.

traditional-family.rationale: Republican civic morality in Rousseau's mould was conventional about family; women excluded from the club; inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic and unaddressed in Jacobin sources, so no position can be reliably inferred from their principles.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Revolutionary force and terror were defended as justice against enemies of liberty.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The Law of Suspects and Revolutionary Tribunal set aside ordinary protections, and Robespierre defended terror as prompt, severe justice.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The Law of the General Maximum fixed grain and staple prices and was enforced by revolutionary armies.

party-controls-media.rationale: Revolutionary government curbed the press in the Terror, but this was done by the state and Convention, not a ruling party; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armies answered to the Convention and Committee of Public Safety through representatives on mission, not to the Club as such; inferred.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Jacobin universalism and the brotherhood of peoples favor welcoming foreigners to citizenship; the period had no stated rule on waiting, inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Jacobin republican virtue condemned officials enriching themselves and favored austere public service; no pay rule is stated, so inferred from Robespierre's rhetoric.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: The Jacobin Club enforced a unified line through purges of members, and Robespierre required unity behind the Committee of Public Safety.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Jacobins held sovereignty to be indivisible and rested in the people of the single French republic, so a binding supranational body contradicts it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Jacobins ruled through the Convention and its committees, and opposed monarchic executive power, with the 1793 Constitution placing the executive under the legislature.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Jacobin line favored the Civil Constitution of the Clergy with elected clergy and later de-Christianization and the Cult of the Supreme Being, against episcopal authority.

clerical-rule.rationale: Jacobins were anticlerical republicans who placed sovereignty in the people and replaced church authority with civic cults.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Jacobins ran the revolutionary war effort, with the levee en masse and the defense of the nation as their first duty.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Robespierre made civic virtue the foundation of the republic, and the Jacobins used festivals, theatre control and censorship to shape republican morals.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Jacobins had no president, and the 1793 Constitution used annual legislative elections; no doctrine addresses re-election of a head of state.

recall-officials.rationale: Popular sovereignty and the right to insurrection imply that the people can discipline their representatives; the 1793 Constitution held its legislators accountable by annual elections, so this is inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Revolutionary France's 1793 constitution renounced wars of conquest and alliances with tyrants; inferred as a rejection of permanent entangling alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Robespierre limited property and favored a wide distribution of it, but did not abolish rent or private ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: The levee en masse and the 1793 constitution's right of insurrection and civic armed duty favored a citizen-army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Robespierre's civic virtue was rooted in the simple, honest people and the republic of small property owners; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Jacobins stressed a single indivisible republic of France, but they did not address divided nations as such.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Jacobins were largely educated lawyers and praised the people's virtue, but not as against the educated; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Jacobins held a universalist civilising mission of the republic and Enlightenment progress over cultural relativism; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: The Terror used execution on a vast scale against enemies of the republic, and Robespierre defended it as justice.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Jacobin republican education was to form virtuous citizens, but sex education and gender equality were not Jacobin aims; anachronistic, and women were excluded from politics.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The Jacobins promoted a civic cult of the Supreme Being and Enlightenment reason, and rejected church doctrine in education.

restrict-pornography.rationale: The Jacobin republic of virtue was austere and moralising, so it would likely restrict obscenity; anachronistic and inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The French republic treated citizens as made by the political community and grew citizenship by law, not by descent alone.

minority-language-support.rationale: The indivisible republic imposed French on the regions, and the Convention in 1794 decreed French as the sole language.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Robespierre and the Jacobins demanded a unified law for all citizens and policed religion as a threat to republican unity.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Jacobin civic virtue demanded conformity to republican values; eccentricity was suspect in the Terror.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The Jacobins did not address foreign debts of poor countries; the issue is anachronistic and no position can be sourced.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Robespierre held that formal political rights meant little without limits on wealth and provision for the poor; inferred from his property and taxation declaration.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The Convention was elected to draft a new republican constitution, and the 1793 Constitution was then put to a popular vote.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Revolutionary government suspended ordinary liberties for the Terror, and Robespierre defended it as necessary to secure the Republic.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Robespierre's declaration speaks of brotherhood among peoples, but this is not a doctrine of aid transfers; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Nuclear weapons are anachronistic; the emphasis on national defense and the levee en masse gives only an inferred lean toward self-reliance.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: The 1793 Constitution had deputies chosen by direct male suffrage but the executive council chosen by the legislature, so direct election of a head of state is not stated; inferred from popular sovereignty.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banking as understood today did not exist, and the Convention directed assignats and the economy through the state, so independence from government is inferred as opposed.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: A historic-homeland claim is anachronistic, though the republic defended France's frontiers in war; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Robespierre's 1793 declaration limits property by the duty not to harm the rights of others and by the needs of society.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; Jacobins favored a republic of small property owners and the label has no place in their thought; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; nothing in the sources bears on it, and Jacobin public-good rhetoric neither favors nor opposes it.

collective-defense.rationale: The 1793 constitution stressed the fraternity of peoples and non-interference, and the Jacobins were wary of standing alliances; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The 1793 constitution renounced conquest and respect for peoples' rights is inferred to cover annexation without consent, though the Republic annexed Belgium.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Jacobins subordinated the clergy to the state and attacked church property, while Robespierre kept a civic religion.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The Republic had no head of state, and the Jacobins were a political party leading the government; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Jacobins crushed the Federalist revolts and the Vendee to preserve the one and indivisible Republic.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Jacobinism is defined by centralisation and indivisible sovereignty, leaving no room for regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The Jacobins abolished the monarchy and executed the king.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Robespierre's declaration called for progressive taxation, the opposite of a flat tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Robespierre's emphasis on public education and civic virtue rests on the view that institutions shape citizens.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Law was the expression of the general will and rulers were bound by it, though revolutionary government suspended the constitution.

space-expansion.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Jacobin priority on public welfare and the Republic's wartime needs.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Indivisible popular sovereignty in a single assembly rejects blending powers between few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Robespierre denounced individual idolatry, though the Jacobins did honor martyrs and a civic cult.

equal-parenting.rationale: Anachronistic; the Jacobins did not address custody, and inferred stances are split.

missingStatements.text: In a national emergency, a government may suspend ordinary legal protections to defeat its internal enemies.
missingStatements.rationale: The Law of Suspects and Revolutionary Tribunal suspended ordinary protections, and Robespierre defended terror as prompt, severe justice.

missingStatements.text: Governments should fix maximum prices for essential foods in times of scarcity.
missingStatements.rationale: The Law of the General Maximum fixed grain and staple prices, enforced by revolutionary armies.

notes: Jacobins were pragmatic on economics: generally pro-market in principle but driven to controls by war. Many answers are low-confidence inferences.
